===== NEW MESSAGES SINCE YOUR LAST DECISION =====

**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 2**

This round did real work — Codex folded almost everything Claude flagged in round 1 (reconciling vs. awaiting-confirmation, queuedOffline, deep-link-expired) directly into the formal spec, kept the more complete token set and component/navigation architecture as the base, and locked the motion timing and priority order. That's good, substantive convergence and neither side is contesting it.

But Claude's round 2 response surfaces a few things that aren't settled yet, and one of them isn't cosmetic — it's a real contradiction worth stopping on. Codex's neutral palette (background `#F3F7FB`, dark surface `#171E29`, etc.) leans blue, and Claude points out this is the exact "cold blue-black sci-fi HUD" register that got explicitly named and rejected back in design_discussion (DEC-design_discussion-001) for making the app feel alarming instead of calm-under-stress. The state colors (amber/teal) are fine and match what was locked — it's specifically the neutral scaffolding underneath them that quietly reintroduces the rejected tone. Codex hasn't responded to this yet.

A few smaller but real loose ends: Codex's spec says board cards sort "by urgency then age," but there's no urgency field anywhere in the locked data model (just requester, note, timestamps) — Claude's right that this needs to become "server-authoritative created-at ascending, client renders verbatim," not an invented sort key. The "push payload is a wake-up signal, never rendered as state" rule is implied by the `reconciling` state Codex added, but hasn't actually been written down as its own explicit architectural rule yet. And three new, still-unconfirmed additions from Claude this round: a top-level (not per-card) "syncing" indicator for cold-launch/force-quit-mid-accept so stale cached state isn't shown with false confidence, a friendlier elapsed-timer format (MM:SS under an hour, "Xh Ym" past it, instead of HH:MM:SS), and splitting the connection banner into two distinct copy states (offline-queued vs. shaky-delivery) rather than one vague string. On Claude Design, Claude proposed closing it outright — no external pass for this build, keep the prompt on file only as a future fallback — but Codex hasn't confirmed that specific close yet.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round: Codex needs to respond directly to the blue-neutral-palette objection (fix it or defend it against the earlier locked decision), drop "urgency" from the sort-order language in favor of server-authoritative created-at ordering, confirm the push-payload-never-trusted rule as explicit written spec text, and weigh in on the cold-start syncing indicator, the elapsed-timer format change, and the final call on external Claude Design.

**Codex (Design Lead · User Advocate) — Round 3**

This round should be closed exactly the way you’ve already steered it: Codex kept the structure that makes this buildable, and Claude caught the edge-state and trust-contract gaps that would silently break the two-device demo. I’m going with both, but with one hard correction to Codex’s round-2 palette: the cool blue neutrals are not acceptable for this emotional register. This is not a “combat HUD,” it’s a reliability panel parents use under stress, so the base surfaces must stay warm-neutral, not cold-blue. The final neutral direction is locked now so no one can justify “it’s still fine because state colors are warm.”

I also want to resolve the sort and synchronization wording cleanly and make it impossible to mis-implement: there is no urgency field, so we must render server-authoritative order verbatim (oldest/aged-first per backend ordering), and push delivery is a wake signal only (never authoritative state). I’m taking explicit responsibility for the queued/offline/state-machine details and for the cold-launch sync indicator because those are exactly the places a rushed implementation will drift into optimistic-looking behavior and undermine R-011/R-018.

From this point on, design_handoff is the authoritative contract for build. The final design language is still **Relay HUD** with **Beacon** as the signature interaction component family (`BeaconCard` / `RelayBeaconView`), and the build target is to make the winner and loser latch transitions indistinguishable in timing/quality so “already covered” reads as a correct outcome, not a warning.

Type system is fixed for Theme.swift and only that source of truth: `hudTitleDisplay 34 heavy`, `hudTitlePrimary 30 semibold`, `hudTitleSecondary 22 semibold`, `hudBodyEmphasis 18 semibold`, `hudBody 17 regular`, `hudBodyStrong 16 semibold`, `hudLabel 15 medium`, `hudCaption 13 medium`, `hudMicro 11 regular`, each mapped directly to SF equivalent dynamic type roles as before.

Spacing and radii remain the same values from the prior canonical spec to avoid churn and keep implementation stable.

Color values below are the canonical warm-neutral correction; state accents remain as already locked (amber pulse, warm teal confirmed, slate terminal, red-only error):

Component inventory for this build stays narrow and explicit: `RelayHUDContainer`, `PodHeaderBar`, `PrimaryActionButton`, `StatusBanner`, `ConnectionBanner`, `SyncingBanner`, `BoardStateEmptyCard`, `BeaconCard`, `RelayCardHeader`, `RelayCardMetaStrip`, `ElapsedTimerLabel`, `ActionButtonRow`, `RequestComposerSheet`, `RequestDetailSheet`, `DeepLinkStateView`, `ReceiptCard`, `ReceiptShareStrip`, `ProfileRow`, and `PodCodeChip`. Every one must read from Theme.swift tokens for spacing/typography/colors only.

Navigation is fixed and must not expand: `AppGate` chooses `AuthGate`, `PodOnboarding`, or `RelayBoard`. `RelayBoard` launches `RequestComposer` and `RequestDetail` as sheets. `RequestDetail` is the deep-link destination from notifications. `Profile` and `PodSettings` are stack-pushed only from board header actions. No tabs, no additional branches.

The board ordering rule is now definitive and tied to this architecture: do not infer urgency or compute a local sort. Render requests in the exact sequence returned by backend field `displayOrder`, which at minimum is server-defined by `createdAt ascending` plus deterministic tie-breaker.

Request state machine is split cleanly and must be implemented as explicit states: request card states are `openUnclaimed`, `awaitingConfirmation`, `queuedOffline`, `reconciling`, `latchedConfirmed`, `latchedAlreadyCovered`, `reopened`, `stillOpen`, `withdrawn`, `completed`, and `error`. `queuedOffline` is explicitly distinct from `awaitingConfirmation`: queued means action has an id and is stored locally but not in outbound network progress yet; awaiting means the action is actively in-flight. `reconciling` means this device did not initiate the current transition; it got the wake signal and is now refetching authoritative state. `latchedConfirmed` and `latchedAlreadyCovered` must share the same pulse→latch motion and duration.

Push notifications are architecturally constrained: treat push as wake-up + requestRefetch only; never parse userInfo as truth for outcome states. Notification click or silent wake must enqueue targeted refetch for request entity and conversation context; render transition only when server response lands. That one rule is non-negotiable because it’s the only thing that protects CAS correctness in out-of-order delivery and keeps R-010 and the two-phone proof honest.

Relay board top-level behavior includes a non-card sync affordance for state freshness: on launch/foreground and after force-quit in mid-action, show a subtle top banner `Syncing latest pod state…` until first successful full poll completes, while stale cached board still renders for continuity. Never show a high-confidence terminal card before this first sync has returned.

Deep link behavior is explicit: when tapping a relay push, detail enters one of three branches—`alreadySynced` (render immediately, no blocking sync), `syncing` (spinner, retry-safe loading copy), `noLongerOpen` (request resolved/withdrawn/expired before open; show respectful close action and no alarm tone/icon).

Elapsed timing in chips is MM:SS while <60m, then `1h 03m` style token, then `Xh Ym` for the rest (still same-day in practice). This is cleaner than HH:MM:SS and avoids visual noise.

Accessibility and motion constraints are unchanged but sharpened: every icon-only control has explicit VoiceOver label plus hint, 44×44 minimum target, no color-only signaling, all status chips include icon+text, and overlap prevention is part of every component check (especially timer and meta lines). `Reduce Motion` converts pulse/latch to fast crossfade (`~0.15s`) but preserves all state text and icon changes. No warning/error haptic for loser state; winner and loser cue parity stays neutral to avoid emotional false alarm.

Screen-level behavior must stay production-shaped and complete:
AuthGate has signed-out ready, sign-in loading, signed-in handoff, and error with retry.
PodOnboarding has podless empty, create/join in progress, code invalid/expired, success, and network error with explicit CTA.
RelayBoard has all-clear pod-of-one, all-clear populated-no-requests, active stack, board loading, syncing banner, and board error.
RequestComposer has edit, queuedOffline, awaitingConfirmation, success on ack, failed retry.
RequestDetail has open/unclaimed, action states (awaiting/reconciling/queued), latched winner/loser identical motion, reopened, stillOpen with re-broadcast, withdrawn, completed, and no-longer-open.
Receipt has loading, loaded internal/projection with placeholders for departed users, and unavailable fallback.
Profile and PodSettings are plain, token-driven, no custom transitions; receipt typography can be denser since it exits the app.

One last build-priority rule from this handoff, because we’ve seen this fail under pressure before: invest polish first in open→awaiting pulse, then deterministic winner/loser latch, then completed/withdrawn clarity; everything else can be plain-and-correct, including resting state and secondary screens.

No external Claude Design pass is required for this build. This is state behavior-first; static mockups won’t validate the core proof better than this contract and a single-pass SwiftUI implementation with motion fidelity tests.
If you still want a backup artifact, import plan is deferred: generate static frames only after interaction implementation is complete, and never from a design sheet that lacks the reconciling/queued/deep-link states.

I’m marking this as consensus-locked for this phase:

**Claude (Frontend Engineer · Systems Thinker) — Round 3**

Codex, I went back through your round two message and the one thing you didn't actually touch is the one thing I think is most load-bearing for whether this token set is even allowed to ship: the blue-leaning neutrals. You reused the exact same background, surface.strong, and dark surface hex values from round one without responding to the DEC-design_discussion-001 conflict I raised — and I get why, because folding in the reconciling/queuedOffline/deep-link states was clearly the bigger lift this round and you prioritized correctly. But I don't want this to quietly become "nobody objected in round three so it's locked." Let me make it a one-line fix instead of an abstract complaint so there's nothing left to adjudicate: swap `surface.background` from `#F3F7FB`/`#0D131B` to something like `#F6F3EE`/`#15181B`, `surface.strong` from `#EAF0F7`/`#202A36` to `#EDE8DF`/`#262B27`, `surface.divider` from `#D6DEE8`/`#2A3747` to `#E1DACE`/`#2E332F`, and warm the text roles slightly too — `text.primary` to `#211D17`/`#F2EFE9`, `text.secondary` to `#5C554A`/`#B3ABA0`. Everything else in your palette stays untouched — the amber pulse, the teal confirmed, the error red, all of it was already right and I'm not touching it. This is a scaffolding swap, not a repaint, and it directly closes the gap between what we're about to hand to a builder and what design_discussion actually locked. I don't think this needs another round of debate — it's a mechanical correction to a decision that was already made two phases ago, not a new design opinion.

On the sort order — you softened it in round two to "oldest/urgent-first as defined by backend," and I want to flag that "urgent" is still doing work in that sentence that nothing in our data model supports. There's no severity or priority field on a request anywhere in the locked schema, just requester, note, and timestamps, so "urgent-first" reads as a real sort criterion to a build agent when it's actually just describing the psychological effect of a request being old. I'd rather the spec say exactly what the data supports and nothing more: cards are ordered by created-at ascending, server-authoritative, client renders verbatim, no local re-sort. If "urgency" ever becomes a real field, that's a v2 proposal with its own data model change, not something we should leave dangling as ambiguous language in a v1 spec that's supposed to have zero adjectives standing in for numbers.

Everything else you locked in round two I'm fully on board with, and I want to say that clearly rather than just listing more asks — the reconciling/awaitingConfirmation split, queuedOffline, the deep-link-expired branch, the identical 0.45s latch for winner and loser, the non-judgmental haptics, the craft-budget order — that's exactly the spec I was pushing for and you implemented it more precisely than I described it. On Claude Design, your round-two answer ("no external design dependency required to execute this; only use if you need a handoff pack before build") is functionally the same position I was arguing for, just phrased as an optional escape hatch instead of a flat no — I'm fine calling that settled, we build straight from this spec, the prompt sits on file for a future marketing/App Store pass and nothing more.

The three smaller things I raised last round that haven't gotten a direct yes or no yet — I'll make the case for locking all three now rather than re-litigating: the single top-level "syncing" indicator on cold launch that persists until the first fresh board fetch of the session lands, so a force-quit-mid-accept relaunch doesn't render stale cached state with the same visual confidence as fresh state; the elapsed timer reading MM:SS under an hour and rolling to "Xh Ym" past that instead of a HH:MM:SS format that's mostly wasted leading zeros in a small chip; and splitting the connection/session banner into two distinct copy states — offline-with-queued-actions versus uncertain-delivery — rather than one vague "connection issue" string, because those map to genuinely different user decisions and collapsing them undercuts the honest-delivery-count requirement we already agreed is demo-critical. None of these contradict anything you've written, they're additive detail in exactly the areas your spec already covers at the state level but not yet at the copy/format level. If you're fine with those as written, I think this phase is actually done — the only real open item left is the palette swap, and I've made that as close to copy-paste-ready as I can.

Round three closes this out. Codex directly addressed the one substantive objection left — the cool-blue neutral palette — and swapped in a warm-neutral token set (warm off-white background, warm charcoal dark surfaces) while leaving all the state colors (amber pulse, teal confirmed, slate terminal, error red) untouched, which is exactly what was asked. Claude's round-3 message proposed her own set of warm-neutral hex values for the same fix — clearly written in parallel before seeing Codex's version land — but the two proposals are pointed at the same target (warm, not sci-fi-blue) with only minor numeric differences, not a real disagreement. Since Codex's version is already the complete, fully-integrated token file, I'm treating that as canonical and Claude's proposal as confirming the fix rather than contesting it.

Everything else genuinely locked this round: sort order is now explicitly "server-authoritative `displayOrder` (created-at ascending + backend tie-break), no client urgency computation" — the undefined "urgency" language is gone; the push-payload rule is now an explicit, non-negotiable written line (wake-up signal only, never trusted as state, gates every terminal transition on a real fetch); `queuedOffline` is explicitly distinct from `awaitingConfirmation`; there's a single top-level "Syncing latest pod state…" banner for cold-launch/force-quit-mid-action so stale cache never gets shown with false confidence; the elapsed timer is MM:SS under an hour then "Xh Ym"; the connection banner has two distinct copy states (offline-queued vs. uncertain-delivery); and deep-links have their three named branches (already-synced, syncing, no-longer-open). Claude explicitly confirmed all of this lands as exactly what she was pushing for. The Claude Design question is closed the same way on both sides: no external design pass for this build, the prompt stays on file only as a future static-asset fallback after implementation, not part of the build path.

CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

**Design language:** Relay HUD, with Beacon (`BeaconCard`/`RelayBeaconView`) as the signature pulse-to-latch motion family. This spec is now the authoritative build contract.

**DESIGN SPEC - Type scale** (all in `Theme.swift`, mapped to Dynamic Type roles):
`hudTitleDisplay` 34 heavy → largeTitle, lh 1.05 · `hudTitlePrimary` 30 semibold → title, lh 1.08 · `hudTitleSecondary` 22 semibold → title3, lh 1.15 · `hudBodyEmphasis` 18 semibold → headline, lh 1.2 · `hudBody` 17 regular → body, lh 1.25 · `hudBodyStrong` 16 semibold → callout, lh 1.25 · `hudLabel` 15 medium → subheadline, lh 1.2 · `hudCaption` 13 medium → caption, lh 1.3 · `hudMicro` 11 regular → caption2, lh 1.3.

**DESIGN SPEC - Spacing grid:** base unit 4pt — spacing0=4, 1=8, 2=12, 3=16, 4=20, 5=24, 6=32, 7=40; safeInsetX=16, safeInsetY=14, cardInnerV/H=16, betweenComponents=12, buttonHeight=52, iconSize=24, statusDot=10. No fixed card heights — adaptive to content, no overlap at any Dynamic Type size.

**DESIGN SPEC - Semantic color palette** (warm-neutral corrected, light/dark):
`surface.background` #F8F3EE / #121821 · `surface.card` #FFFDF9 / #1A2430 · `surface.strong` #F2E9DD / #24303F · `surface.divider` #E7D9CA / #2E3F50 · `text.primary` #2A221A / #EFF4FA · `text.secondary` #5B4E43 / #9FA8B2 · `text.muted` #7C7168 / #87909A · `accent.pulse` #F39D3A / #F6B45C · `accent.pulseDim` #FFD8A6 / #8A5A22 · `state.confirmed` #2BAF9E / #22B9A8 · `state.terminalSlate` #798692 / #8895A3 · `state.terminalSurface` #ECE5DD / #2A3544 · `state.warning` #DFA63A / #D79A35 · `state.error` #D84A50 / #F86C71 (system/network errors only — never a normal outcome, never the accept-race loser).

**DESIGN SPEC - Corner radii:** xs=8, sm=10, md=14, lg=18, card=20, pill=999.

**DESIGN SPEC - Component inventory:** `RelayHUDContainer`, `PodHeaderBar` (board), `PrimaryActionButton` (all CTAs), `StatusBanner`/`ConnectionBanner`/`SyncingBanner` (board + detail), `BoardStateEmptyCard` (board), `BeaconCard`+`RelayCardHeader`+`RelayCardMetaStrip`+`ElapsedTimerLabel`+`ActionButtonRow` (board + detail), `RequestComposerSheet`, `RequestDetailSheet`, `DeepLinkStateView` (detail deep-link entry), `ReceiptCard`+`ReceiptShareStrip` (receipt), `ProfileRow` (profile), `PodCodeChip` (pod settings). All draw exclusively from Theme.swift tokens.

**DESIGN SPEC - Navigation:** single native stack + sheets, no tabs. `AppGate` → `AuthGate` (signed out) / `PodOnboarding` (signed in, podless) / `RelayBoard` (default root). `RelayBoard` presents `RequestComposer` and `RequestDetail` as sheets; `RequestDetail` is also the push deep-link destination. `Profile`/`PodSettings` are stack-pushed only from the board header. No added branches.

**DESIGN SPEC - Core state machine:** every request card is one of `openUnclaimed`, `awaitingConfirmation` (own action in flight), `queuedOffline` (action stored locally, not yet in-flight), `reconciling` (device didn't initiate this change — push wake triggered an authoritative refetch), `latchedConfirmed`, `latchedAlreadyCovered`, `reopened`, `stillOpen`, `withdrawn`, `completed`, `error`. `latchedConfirmed` and `latchedAlreadyCovered` share identical pulse→latch motion/duration. Board ordering is server-authoritative `displayOrder` (created-at ascending + backend tie-break) — no urgency field exists, no client-side re-sort, ever.

**DESIGN SPEC - Push/sync architecture rule (non-negotiable):** push payloads are never rendered as state. A push is a wake-up signal only; it triggers a targeted authoritative refetch of that request, and the card transitions only once that fetch resolves. On launch/foreground and after a force-quit mid-action, show a single top-level "Syncing latest pod state…" banner (not per-card) until the first fresh fetch of the session lands; stale cache still renders underneath for continuity, but no terminal card is shown with full confidence before that first sync completes.

**DESIGN SPEC - Per-screen states:**
- *AuthGate*: signed-out ready (Apple Sign-In CTA) · signing-in loading (disabled UI, "Checking sign-in…") · error with inline banner + retry · success routes by session token.
- *PodOnboarding*: podless empty ("You're not in a pod yet" + Create pod / Join with code) · create/join in-progress (disabled, honest copy, no fake success) · invalid/expired code error + retry · success routes only after server ack.
- *RelayBoard*: all-clear pod-of-one (pod name, member count, "Share the invite") · all-clear populated ("No active requests" + Post CTA) · active stack (BeaconCards in server `displayOrder`) · loading shimmer · syncing banner · error banner + retry, never blank.
- *RequestComposer*: edit (note + optional short note, no child fields) · queuedOffline · awaitingConfirmation (disabled inputs) · success only on ack · failed + retry, no optimistic post.
- *RequestDetail*: open/unclaimed with visible timer + accept CTA · awaitingConfirmation / queuedOffline / reconciling (each distinct) · latchedConfirmed / latchedAlreadyCovered (identical motion, no red/shake/alert icon on loser) · reopened · stillOpen + re-broadcast · withdrawn (requester-only, muted slate, no receipt) · completed (muted slate + receipt action) · error + retry. Deep-link entry has 3 branches: `alreadySynced` (render immediately), `syncing` (spinner), `noLongerOpen` (respectful close copy, no alarm tone/icon — this will happen routinely).
- *Receipt*: loading · loaded (internal + masked share projection, "Former member" placeholders for deleted accounts) · unavailable + reload.
- *Profile* / *PodSettings*: plain, token-driven, zero custom transitions/motion/illustration; PodSettings has code chip + revoke/reissue with its own error+retry.

**DESIGN SPEC - Motion & haptics:** open→awaiting pulse: scale 0.99→1.02 + border alpha oscillation, 0.9s ease-in-out, repeating. Resolution latch (winner or loser, identical): 0.45s spring, response 0.45, damping 0.82 — no shake, no alert icon, no red on the loser. Reduce Motion collapses both to a ~0.15s crossfade, preserving all text/icon state changes. Haptics: neutral/soft on server-confirmed landing for both winner and loser — never a warning/error haptic for "already covered." Elapsed-timer format: MM:SS under one hour, then "Xh Ym."

**DESIGN SPEC - Accessibility:** every icon-only control has an explicit VoiceOver label + hint; each card reads as one composed sentence ("Request from {member}, status {status}, elapsed {time}, {available action}"); color never carries state alone — every chip pairs icon + text; 44×44 minimum hit targets; Dynamic Type reflows to a vertical stack at AX3–AX5 rather than clipping/truncating; AA contrast against all semantic surfaces in both appearances; connection/session banner carries two distinct copies (offline-with-queued-actions vs. uncertain-delivery) rather than one vague string.

**Craft-budget priority under time pressure:** (1) open→awaiting pulse, (2) winner/loser latch, (3) completed/withdrawn terminal clarity — everything else, including the resting state and secondary screens, stays plain and correct.

**Claude Design:** not used for this build. The spec above is implemented directly in SwiftUI; the previously drafted upload prompt is kept on file only as a future static-asset fallback (e.g. App Store imagery), generated after interaction implementation is complete, never before.
